# Idempotency/recovery record looked up by a non-idempotency key (P0)

Pattern: a recovery/idempotency record store is keyed by operation_id on write, but the read path looks it up by another attribute (e.g. workspace) via a linear scan. Records are never pruned, so the first completed record for that attribute matches every later request. New operations then skip apply and still return ok — a silent lost update. A related symptom: the read and write keys don't match, so a reused operation_id from another scope overwrites that scope's record.

Detection: idempotency lookup that doesn't match on the idempotency key; `next(... for item in store.values() if item[<non-key>] == ...)`; the response built from request args instead of the matched record/receipt (this hides the mismatch from tests).

Fix: read and write by the same key (operation_id, or a composite (scope, operation_id)); short-circuit completed records before side-effecting calls; reject a reused key with a different payload; add a test for two operation_ids on the same scope.

Seen in: service.py save() (save recovery update), 2026-10-11.
